message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity is exact for both candidates (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all corneal dystrophy) and both come from the same UKB portability paper with similar training N, covariates, and European-selected validation record. With no AUC/R2 reported for either, the only comparable performance signal is partial correlation, where PGS002042 is higher (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384). As a structural tie-breaker within the same study/endpoint, PGS002042 also uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (59,944 vs 38), which is generally a stronger genome-wide PRS construction than a very sparse penalized-regression score when other factors are held constant. Trait heritability lookup returned no matching EUR h2 records for corneal dystrophy, so h2 cannot further contextualize the observed partial-r; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS000013 is a direct match to the target (trait_efo coronary artery disease; phenotyping_reported “Coronary artery disease”), whereas several high-AUC alternatives are on narrower or shifted endpoints (e.g., recurrent events, familial hypercholesterolemia subset, carotid plaque, coronary calcium, acute coronary syndrome). Performance evidence quality: per the performance-metrics guidance, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only / covariate-adjusted PRS contribution) are more informative than full-model AUROC alone. PGS000013 reports a PRS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.04 (and full-model AUROC=0.81 with only basic covariates: age/sex/PCs/chip), giving clearer evidence of standalone PRS signal than candidates reporting only covariate-inflated full-model AUROC/C-index. Study scale/structure: large training sample (n=120,280) and large European validation (n=288,978) support robustness. Heritability sanity check: local EUR CAD h2 estimates are ~0.065–0.096 (liability ~0.067–0.115); a PRS-only R2 of 0.04 is plausible relative to this ceiling and does not suggest metric misuse, supporting interpretability of the reported PRS contribution."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001254","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint fidelity is direct for all three candidates (Dupuytren contracture / palmar fascia contracture; same EFO), so selection hinges on usable, comparable performance evidence and evaluation context. PGS001254 reports both PRS-only and full-model discrimination (PGS-only AUROC=0.6646; full-model AUROC=0.7413; incremental AUROC=0.0447) with clear covariates and a large European validation sample (n=67,425), making its standalone PGS performance directly interpretable. By contrast, PGS001880 and PGS002092 (same publication family) only report partial correlation (partial-r ~0.078–0.080) without AUROC/R², limiting comparability and practical interpretability for a binary disease endpoint in this selection. Although PGS002092 has far more variants and slightly higher partial-r than PGS001880, the lack of standard metrics keeps them less actionable than PGS001254 for a ‘best PGS’ pick. Heritability sanity-check: no matching local h2 records were found for ‘dupuytren contracture’ / ‘Dupuytren’s contracture’, so h2 cannot be used to contextualize the reported R²/AUROC; the decision is therefore based on the candidate metadata and metric completeness/clarity per the evaluator guidance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS005271","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity is acceptable across all candidates (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis, a close synonym). None report PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is available with covariates listed as Unknown, so cross-model ranking by AUROC is weak per the performance-metrics guidance. Using the fallback signals from the performance_metrics skill section, PGS005271 is preferred because it uses a modern Bayesian shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~1.09M) and shows the strongest per-SD effect size evidence (OR≈1.55) among the PRS-CS models, while its full-model AUROC (0.630) is similar to PGS005270 (0.639) and higher than PGS005272 (0.605), differences that are likely not meaningful without PRS-only metrics. Heritability sanity-check was attempted via get_heritability_records(\"Hashimoto's thyroiditis\"), but no matching EUR h2 records were returned, so no h2-based interpretation could be applied."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000639","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: Target is Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Among candidates, PGS000637/638/639/640 are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have coherent phenotyping_reported (“Hodgkin’s disease”), whereas several other candidates are for non-Hodgkin lymphoma or other hematologic malignancies (trait mismatch per trait-label guidance). Performance evidence (interpreted cautiously as full-model, not PRS-only): within the direct-match Hodgkin set, PGS000639 has the strongest reported discrimination package (full-model AUROC 0.62; Nagelkerke pseudo-R² 0.0276; OR per SD 1.476) compared with PGS000638 (AUROC 0.601; R² 0.0193; OR 1.377) and PGS000637/640 (AUROC ~0.57; lower R² and OR). Covariates are similar across these four (age, sex, batch, PCs), improving comparability. Method/structure: although PRS-CS/lassosum use many variants, in this specific evaluation PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) shows better validated performance than the denser methods, so it is preferred given the fixed candidate list. Heritability sanity-check: local h2 lookup for “hodgkins lymphoma” returned only non-Hodgkin lymphoma self-report matches (no direct Hodgkin record), so h2 cannot strongly calibrate expectations here; this lowers confidence but does not overturn the direct-match, best-performing Hodgkin candidate selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000114","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: The target is broad juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). Per the trait-label guidance, phenotyping_reported is primary; PGS000114 has phenotyping_reported = Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and trait_efo matches the umbrella disease, whereas PGS000324/325/326 are subtype-only endpoints (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular) and are therefore weaker matches for a generic JIA target unless a subtype is explicitly desired.

Performance/covariates interpretation: None of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is available, which the performance-metrics guidance treats as non-comparable for cross-model ranking. Given similar basic covariates across all (sex, PCs 1–10), the safest choice is the best endpoint match rather than chasing a higher full-model AUROC from a subtype model (e.g., 0.93 for enthesitis-related JIA).

Heritability sanity check: A trait-specific h2 lookup for “juvenile idiopathic arthritis” returned no matching EUR records, so no heritability-based ceiling check can be applied here; this lowers confidence but does not change the endpoint-driven selection.

Overall: PGS000114 is the only direct umbrella JIA score in the fixed list and is therefore the best match for the requested target trait."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003586","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: Target trait is preeclampsia. PGS003586 has trait_reported “Pre-eclampsia”, trait_efo “preeclampsia”, and phenotyping_reported “Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia”, which is the most direct match among candidates. By contrast, PGS003587 is labeled “Gestational hypertension” (despite trait_efo preeclampsia) and PGS004593 has phenotyping_reported “Gestational hypertension”, which is a related but not identical endpoint (per trait-label guidance, phenotyping_reported is primary). Performance evidence: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2; therefore, per performance-metrics guidance, effect size magnitude is the best available discriminator. PGS003586 shows a stronger per-SD effect (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.24–1.38) than PGS003587 (OR=1.20) and is at least as directly relevant as PGS004593 (HR=1.16 on a gestational-hypertension phenotype). Study/package signals: PGS003586 comes from a recent, disease-focused Nat Med multi-cohort effort using PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants and European evaluation (n=25,582) with only basic covariates (age, age^2, PCs), which is a clean and comparable setup. Heritability sanity check: a lookup for EUR heritability records for “preeclampsia” returned no matching records, so no h2-based ceiling check can be applied here; selection is therefore based on endpoint fidelity plus the strongest available effect-size evidence."}
